articles.title: 'A number of players playing for their careers': Simon Katich blasts batting approach as Australia fight to save 2nd Test
articles.summary: Australia are under pressure in the second Test against South Africa, with former batter Simon Katich warning that several players could be fighting to
articles.body: Australia are under pressure in the second Test against South Africa, with former batter Simon Katich warning that several players could be fighting to save their places in the team. Marnus Labuschagne, Nic Maddinson and Beau Webster have struggled in the match, leaving Australia with plenty to prove on the final day in Gqeberha.Australia were 156/4 at the end of Day 4 after being asked to follow on, still trailing South Africa by 170 runs. Labuschagne scored 39 before throwing away his wicket with an attacking shot against spinner Simon Harmer. Despite getting starts in recent matches, the batter has struggled to convert them into big scores.Katich questioned Labuschagne’s decision to play an aggressive shot when Australia were trying to save the match. "There are a number of players playing for their careers in this innings," Katich said on SEN radio.He added, "Only he knows what was going through his mind when he tried to take Harmer down the ground, against the breeze, when Australia are trying to play for a draw."Katich also questioned how selectors would view the dismissal, pointing out that Labuschagne had received several opportunities over the years.Labuschagne under pressure as Australia fight backAustralia head coach Andrew McDonald was also disappointed with Labuschagne’s latest failure. The 32-year-old has not scored a Test century since July 2023 and continues to struggle to turn promising starts into substantial innings."I feel like I am on repeat" McDonald said, reflecting on Labuschagne’s repeated scores in the 30s.He added that Australia had built a useful partnership and were beginning to recover before Labuschagne’s dismissal. "When you do that hard work, you've got to cash in, and unfortunately, that wasn't to be the case for Marn. We were disappointed, and he will be too," the coach said.South Africa close in as pressure mountsAustralia lead the three-match series 1-0 after winning the first Test at Kingsmead by 214 runs. However, South Africa have fought back strongly in Gqeberha, declaring at 425/9 before dismissing Australia for just 99 in their first innings.Rain limited play during the first two days, but South Africa have put themselves in a strong position to win the match. Travis Head, unbeaten on 87, and nightwatchman Scott Boland will resume Australia's innings on the final day.Australia's team management could face further scrutiny if the visitors lose, particularly after Nathan Lyon's omission from the playing XI drew criticism.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt handed two-match ban for medication breach
articles.summary: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt has been handed a two-match suspension for failing to comply with requirements governing the use of prescription
articles.body: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt has been handed a two-match suspension for failing to comply with requirements governing the use of prescription medication, Cricket Australia (CA) said on Thursday.The 33-year-old will miss Australia's third and final T20I against New Zealand at North Sydney Oval on Thursday, as well as Adelaide Strikers' opening match of the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) against Melbourne Stars on October 31.Cricket Australia clarified that the breach involved a single incident that occurred outside competition and was not related to performance enhancement. The suspension applies to both international and domestic cricket.Cricket Australia clarifies nature of breachIn a statement, CA said the offence involved non-compliance with its medical guidelines governing prescription medication."The breach was a failure to adhere to requirements under the Sports Science and Sports Medicine guidelines with regard to prescription medication," Cricket Australia said.The governing body also stressed that the incident was isolated and had occurred outside the competitive environment."This (breach) relates to a single incidence which occurred while out of competition and was not for performance enhancing purposes," CA added.The suspension means Schutt will be unavailable for Australia's series-deciding T20I against New Zealand and will also miss the beginning of her domestic campaign with Adelaide Strikers.Schutt accepts sanction and apologisesSchutt accepted the suspension and apologised for not meeting the standards expected of players representing Australian cricket."I fully accept the penalty handed down and apologise for failing to meet the standards expected of me. I'm sorry for the attention this has caused and appreciate the support I've received," Schutt said in her statement.The fast bowler acknowledged that players were regularly educated about the relevant guidelines and accepted responsibility for complying with them."While this occurred out of competition and was not performance related, I understand that I am responsible for following the Sports Science and Sports Medicine Guidelines, which players receive regular education on, and I should have adhered to these guidelines," she added.CA said it would continue to provide appropriate support to Schutt while reinforcing the standards and responsibilities expected of everyone representing the game.Suspension follows impressive ODI seriesThe ban comes after Schutt enjoyed an outstanding ODI series against Bangladesh, finishing as Player of the Series after taking 10 wickets at an average of 7.1.Her absence is a setback for Australia ahead of the final T20I against New Zealand, while Adelaide Strikers will also have to manage without the experienced pacer for their WBBL opener.The suspension is limited to two matches, with CA's statement making clear that the incident was not related to performance-enhancing purposes.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: First time in history! India bowlers make unwanted record as New Zealand run riot
articles.summary: For the first time in men’s T20I cricket, five Indian bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in an innings as New Zealand piled up 225/8 in the first T20I in
articles.body: For the first time in men’s T20I cricket, five Indian bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in an innings as New Zealand piled up 225/8 in the first T20I in Christchurch on Thursday. The hosts took advantage of India's struggles with the ball, with Finn Allen scoring 45 off 24 balls and Glenn Phillips remaining unbeaten on 82 off 40.The feat had occurred 13 times overall in men’s T20Is, but this was the first instance involving five Indian bowlers in the same innings. Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceded 49 runs in four overs, Arshdeep Singh gave away 45, Mayank Yadav 40, Axar Patel 51 and Nitish Reddy 40.New Zealand's total was the joint-highest against India in T20Is and their highest on home soil.With Jasprit Bumrah not part of the squad, the Indian attack struggled to contain the hosts despite some early swing on offer. New Zealand's openers dealt with the movement before taking on the bowlers, with Tim Seifert scoring 24 off 17 balls.Bhuvneshwar, playing his first international match in nearly four years, began with a decent first over. However, Seifert hit him for two fours and a six over long-on in his next over, which cost India 17 runs.Allen then attacked Arshdeep in the following over, which also went for 17 runs, giving New Zealand momentum in the powerplay. The openers were particularly effective at finding boundaries on the off-side.Mayank was brought into the attack during the powerplay and gave India a breakthrough when Seifert was caught behind off the final ball of the fifth over.Axar was handed the final over of the powerplay, but the left-arm spinner conceded two sixes. Allen cleared long-off before Daryl Mitchell stepped out and sent the ball over the long-on boundary. New Zealand reached 65/1 in the first six overs.Arshdeep dismissed Mitchell in his second spell, but Bhuvneshwar continued to struggle. His third over cost 14 runs before he was given the responsibility of bowling the final over, which also went for 14. He finished with figures of 0/49 in four overs.Phillips remained unbeaten and finished the innings with a switch hit over cover. Bevon Jacobs also made an impact with 31 off 16 balls, including a first-ball six down the ground off Arshdeep.New Zealand scored 67 runs in the final five overs to cross the 200-run mark, putting India's bowling attack under pressure throughout the innings.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma set a new record for hitting the first ball he faced for a six most often in T20Is, but India had a huge target to chase after New Zealand
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma set a new record for hitting the first ball he faced for a six most often in T20Is, but India had a huge target to chase after New Zealand posted 225/8 in the opening T20I in Christchurch on Thursday.Chasing 226, Abhishek faced his first delivery off the final ball of the first over and sent Matt Henry over the cover boundary for a six. Henry bowled a full delivery wide of off stump, but Abhishek went through with his lofted drive and cleared the ropes to reach the milestone.Abhishek has now hit the first ball he faced for a six seven times in T20Is, moving ahead of Afghanistan's Shafiqullah Shinwari, who has done so six times. Suryakumar Yadav is third on the list with five such sixes, while Ireland's Paul Stirling, New Zealand's Colin Munro and the UAE's Mohammad Naveed have managed it four times each.Most sixes off the first ball faced in T20Is7 — Abhishek Sharma (India)6 — Shafiqullah Shinwari (Afghanistan)5 — Suryakumar Yadav (India)4 — Paul Stirling (Ireland)4 — Colin Munro (New Zealand)4 — Mohammad Naveed (UAE)Abhishek and Sanju Samson gave India the quick start they needed, putting together 93 runs for the opening wicket in just 5.5 overs. However, Michael Bracewell ended the partnership by dismissing Abhishek for 29 off 12 balls. The left-hander struck three sixes and two fours during his brief innings.The partnership also saw Abhishek and Samson equal the record for the most 50-plus opening stands by an Indian pair in T20Is in a calendar year. Their stand was their fifth such partnership in 2026, putting them alongside two other Indian pairs on the list.Most 50-plus opening stands for India in a calendar year in T20Is5 — KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma (2021)5 — Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill (2025)5 — Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson (2026)4 — Shikhar Dhawan and Rohit Sharma (2018)Earlier, Finn Allen and Glenn Phillips led New Zealand to 225/8, the joint-highest total against India in T20Is and New Zealand's highest on home soil. Allen scored 45 off 24 balls, while Phillips remained unbeaten on 82 off 40 deliveries.With Jasprit Bumrah not part of the squad, India's bowlers struggled to contain the hosts. Despite some early swing, New Zealand's batters found ways to score freely, adding 67 runs in the final five overs.Axar Patel was India's most expensive bowler, conceding 51 runs in four overs. The innings also brought an unwanted record for India, as five bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in a T20I innings for the first time. It was the 13th such instance in men's T20Is overall.Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceded 49 runs in his four overs, Arshdeep Singh gave away 45, Mayank Yadav and Nitish Reddy conceded 40 each, while Axar finished with figures of 1/51.At the time of writing the story, India were 128/4 in 11 overs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: One frame at a time! Story of Multan's Minhas brothers through their father's lens
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Kashif Minhas has captured thousands of photographs of cricketers over the years.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Kashif Minhas has captured thousands of photographs of cricketers over the years. He is also an avid birdwatcher who sometimes waits for hours to get that perfect shot. But when his sons are playing and he is busy behind the lens on the ground, the avid shutterbug finds it difficult to keep his nerves in check."I have thousands of photographs of international cricketers. When I am completely focused on a match, I become very attentive to every ball. Capturing a catch at the right moment is special. However, these days, when my sons are playing, I sometimes enjoy watching the cricket live more than photographing it," Kashif Minhas, who runs a car business in Multan for a living, tells TimesofIndia.com.Earlier this year, Kashif was caught on camera by the broadcasters after his elder son, Arafat Minhas, playing only his third ODI, got out against Australia at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. As Arafat was dismissed, Kashif, standing behind the boundary rope with his camera, could not hold back his emotions."I was clicking his photographs, and the moment he got out, I put my hand on the camera and lowered my head. The television cameras caught that reaction, and it went viral," he says.The world doesn't know about my third son, Abdullah Minhas. He is immensely talented as well. He is a left-handed top-order batter and a right-arm leg-break bowler. He has been selected at the Under-17 level and is working hard."They [the broadcasters] know I am his father, so they often keep a camera on me. I even asked the director not to focus on me because I did not want to be shown in front of everyone. People think I am an official photographer of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), which I am not. I freelance for a local newspaper, Daily Pakistan. But they told me that the visual had helped them garner a lot of views, so I thought, 'Chalo, kisi ka toh bhala ho raha' (At least someone is benefiting from it)," he adds.Kashif, however, was deeply hurt by the false stories that circulated after the visuals went viral."That story made me sad. We have been in the car business since 1980, and I have a large showroom in Multan. Some people portrayed the story as if we belonged to a poor family and I had started photographing my children because we had run out of money. That is not the case. Photography is just my hobby. I have a very good car business and import cars from Japan. I never needed money to fund my children's cricket," he says.Kashif's two sons, Arafat Minhas and Sameer Minhas, have shown the world what they are capable of. Arafat has played five ODIs and seven T20Is for Pakistan. The all-rounder has already taken two five-wicket hauls, one each against Australia and England, in his brief international career. Sameer Minhas has lit up age-group cricket, and one cannot forget his 172 off 113 balls against India in the 2025 U-19 Asia Cup final.Kashif says his third son is also getting ready."The world doesn't know about my third son, Abdullah Minhas. He is immensely talented as well. He is a left-handed top-order batter and a right-arm leg-break bowler. He has been selected at the Under-17 level and is working hard," says a proud father.Like many fathers in the subcontinent, Kashif, too, is a cricket tragic."I was also a cricketer. I represented my regional team in Multan. But my father asked me to quit cricket and focus on the family business. He told me to leave cricket or leave home. I left home for two or three days, but then my mother asked me to come back and give up cricket. Nothing is more important to me than my mother, so I quit," he recalls.But one fine day, while playing with a tape ball in their car porch, Kashif's eyes lit up when he saw Arafat and Sameer, then aged nine and seven, respectively, cutting, driving and pulling.When I saw my children playing, I immediately realised that they had something special in them. I decided that what had happened to me should not happen to them. I wanted them to have the opportunity to pursue cricket."The floor was wet, and their hand-eye coordination was amazing. When I saw my children playing, I immediately realised that they had something special in them. I decided that what had happened to me should not happen to them. I wanted them to have the opportunity to pursue cricket," he says."I took them to a local cricket academy, and when I saw how well they were playing against pace, I began to take their cricket more seriously. Arafat performed well in the PCB Under-13 tournament, then at the Under-16 and Under-19 levels. Sameer followed in his footsteps, and soon Abdullah will do the same. We kept trying and praying, and Allah blessed us," he adds.Kashif, who had to give up his own cricketing ambitions, acknowledges that cricket is a tough sport to succeed in and requires much more than time and money."It requires a lot of dedication. You have to make sacrifices. I was away with my children for their training when I heard the news of my father's death. After his demise, I had to spend a lot of time at the office. But whenever they played matches outside Multan, I would travel and sit at the ground from morning until evening," he recalls.As his sons progressed through age-group cricket, Kashif came up with the idea of taking up photography as a way to stay close to them. He started freelancing and soon found work with a local daily. As Arafat and Sameer began making waves with their performances, Kashif, too, became a familiar face on cricket grounds across Pakistan, camera in hand."It was an amazing moment for me," says Kashif, recalling Arafat's ODI debut against Australia in Rawalpindi."I never imagined that a day would come when my children would represent Pakistan in international cricket and I would be on the ground photographing them. It felt like a blessing, and I was very happy that day. He [Arafat] performed well in the last match [against England]," he further adds.Kashif has never been harsh on his sons regarding cricket. But he has one dream he hopes to fulfil through them: winning an ICC trophy."I was never harsh on them. When they were not performing well, I would tell them that it was not their day and that their time would come. I would encourage them to stay prepared for the next opportunity. I never wanted to put unnecessary pressure on them. But I will be even happier when my children win an ICC trophy for their country," he says.The Minhas family could have etched its name in the Guinness World Records, with members representing Pakistan at different age-group levels. But the PCB has declined a request from the over-50s team to participate in the International Masters Cricket World Cup, which is being hosted by India in January next year. Minhas Sr was a member of that squad. Pakistan won the previous edition of the tournament, held in Sri Lanka last year, but this time the board has informed the Pakistan Veterans Cricket Association that its team will not be permitted to travel to India and participate."It would have been great to represent Pakistan, but it's okay. I will get the chance later," he says.For Kashif Minhas, cricket has come full circle. He once had to abandon his own ambitions at his father's insistence, but he made sure his sons had the freedom to pursue theirs. Today, he watches them represent Pakistan, capturing their highs and lows through his lens while carrying the hopes of a father who knows what it means to let go of a dream. An ICC trophy would be the ultimate reward, but for Kashif, seeing his sons live the dream he once had to give up is already a journey worth cherishing.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Sanju Samson continued his consistent run in T20Is this year with a 67 off 33 balls as India pulled off their highest successful chase in T20 cricket, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the first match of the five-game series in Christchurch on Thursday.Chasing 226, India got off to a flying start but lost their way in the middle overs before captain Shreyas Iyer and Naman Dhir helped them cross the finish line with two balls to spare. Shreyas scored 42, while Naman remained unbeaten on 42 off just 15 deliveries.Highest successful chases for India in T20Is226 vs NZ, Christchurch, 2026209 vs AUS, Visakhapatnam, 2023209 vs NZ, Raipur, 2026208 vs WI, Hyderabad, 2019207 vs SL, Mohali, 2009204 vs NZ, Auckland, 2020The second T20I will also be played at Hagley Oval on Saturday.India looked in control after racing to 94/1 in the powerplay, with Samson leading the charge. However, New Zealand spinners Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell brought the hosts back into the game, as India lost three wickets for seven runs. From 93 without loss, the visitors slipped to 122/4 in the 11th over.The long boundaries also played a part in India's middle-order collapse, with Ishan Kishan and Tilak Varma losing their wickets while attempting to clear the ropes.Samson, however, had already given India the platform they needed. He struck eight fours and four sixes in his 67, registering his eighth score of 50 or more in 26 innings this year. He targeted the straight boundary regularly, with his flick off Lockie Ferguson over long-on standing out.Abhishek Sharma supported Samson during their 93-run opening partnership, scoring 29 off 12 balls. He pulled Adam Milne for two consecutive sixes in the fourth over as India raced towards the target.With the chase in danger of slipping away, Shreyas took responsibility and kept India in contention. He also benefited from a reprieve when Finn Allen dropped a difficult catch in the 15th over. India needed 55 runs from the final 30 balls, with five wickets remaining.Naman joined Shreyas and struck timely boundaries to ease the pressure. Their contributions proved enough to take India over the line in a tense finish.Earlier, New Zealand posted 225/8 after being asked to bat, with Finn Allen scoring 45 off 24 balls and Glenn Phillips making an unbeaten 82 off 40. The total was New Zealand's highest on home soil and the joint-highest score against India in T20Is.Despite some early swing, the New Zealand openers found ways to score freely. Tim Seifert, who made 24 off 17 balls, attacked Bhuvneshwar Kumar after the Indian pacer bowled a decent first over. Seifert struck two fours and a six over long-on in Bhuvneshwar's next over, which cost 17 runs.Allen then attacked Arshdeep Singh, helping New Zealand build momentum in the powerplay. Mayank Yadav gave India a breakthrough when Seifert was caught behind off the final ball of the fifth over.Axar Patel, bowling the last over of the powerplay, conceded two sixes as Allen cleared long-off and Daryl Mitchell stepped out to hit over long-on. New Zealand reached 65/1 in the first six overs.Arshdeep later dismissed Mitchell, but India's bowlers struggled to contain the scoring. Bhuvneshwar conceded 49 runs without taking a wicket in four overs, while Axar gave away 51. Bevon Jacobs added 31 off 16 balls, including a first-ball six down the ground off Arshdeep, before Phillips finished the innings with a switch hit over cover.New Zealand scored 67 runs in the final five overs, setting India a target of 226. articles.title: Joe Root creates history! Becomes first England batter to cross 8,000-run mark in ODIs
articles.summary: Joe Root etched his name in the record books on Thursday, becoming the first England batter to cross 8,000 runs in One-Day Internationals during the clash
articles.body: Joe Root etched his name in the record books on Thursday, becoming the first England batter to cross 8,000 runs in One-Day Internationals during the clash against Sri Lanka in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series.The experienced right-hander reached the landmark with a fluent knock of 69 off 66 deliveries, striking eight fours. He achieved the feat in his 186th ODI innings, further underlining his consistency in the 50-over format.Root's latest innings took his career tally to 8,005 runs in 197 matches at an average of 50.66 and a strike rate of 87.83. His record also includes 20 centuries and 49 half-centuries, with a highest score of 166.Root leads England's ODI run-scoring chartsRoot's achievement puts him comfortably ahead of the other leading run-scorers in England's ODI history. Former captain Eoin Morgan occupied second place with 6,957 runs from 225 matches, leaving a gap of 1,048 runs between the two.Jos Buttler follows with 5,678 runs, while Ian Bell (5,416) and Paul Collingwood (5,092) complete the top five. Root also leads the group in career average and centuries, reflecting his ability to deliver substantial contributions across different stages of his career.Since making his ODI debut against India in Rajkot in 2013, Root has established himself as one of England's most dependable batters. His ability to combine consistency with the capacity to build long innings has made him a key figure in the side's batting line-up.A consistent run-scorer across formatsRoot's productivity has extended well beyond ODIs. In 2015 and 2016, he set consecutive records for the most runs scored by an England player across all formats in a calendar year, registering 2,228 and 2,570 runs respectively.In 2016, he also came within five runs of Michael Vaughan's England record of 1,481 Test runs in a calendar year, set in 2002.Root was appointed England's Test captain in 2017 following Alastair Cook's resignation. During the second half of that decade, he continued to make significant contributions in ODIs, scoring more than 900 runs in each of three consecutive years from 2017 to 2019.He stepped away from the 50-over format in 2020 but returned in 2023 ahead of the ODI World Cup in India. Although England endured a disappointing campaign, Root contributed three half-centuries.His latest milestone adds another chapter to an international career built on consistency and adaptability, establishing him as the first English batter to reach the 8,000-run mark in ODIs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sri Lanka chase 430 to beat England despite Harry Brook 202
articles.summary: Harry Brook’s first double century by an England batter in a one-day international is not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pull off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi.
articles.body:
One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi

England 429-4 (50 overs): Brook 202, Root 69, Jacks 66*

Sri Lanka 430-8 (49.5 overs): Rathnayake 130, Avishka 97, Shanaka 97

Harry Brook's first double century by an England batter in a one-day international was not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pulled off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi.

Brook passed Ben Stokes' previous England best score of 182 and posted the fastest ODI double hundred, off 114 balls, in his astonishing 202.

In clobbering the 14th double-hundred in a men's one-day international and the 12th highest individual score, Brook lifted England to 429-4 – at halfway the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan.

But Sri Lanka, who chose to bat second, were not deterred, even when they were reduced to 24-2. They set about completing the second-highest successful chase in ODI history.

Pavan Rathnayake made a sublime 130, while Aviksha Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both added 97.

With Jofra Archer rested for the tri-series and leg-spinner Adil Rashid left out of this match for tactical reasons, England's bowling was woeful. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs from his nine overs.

Up with the required rate throughout their innings, Sri Lanka needed 109 from the final 10 overs and were able to absorb the losses of Rathnayake and Shanaka.

Sri Lanka needed eight off the final over, sent down by Josh Tongue, who was pinpoint with his accuracy to bowl Dinuth Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries.

But in a sensational finish, Janith Liyanage, the man bowling when Brook reached 200, would not be denied.

With six needed from two balls, Liyanage pummelled Tongue's penultimate delivery of the match down the ground for a match-winning maximum, sparking joyous Sri Lankan celebrations.

One of the most incredible one-day internationals ever played ended with an aggregate of 847 runs, behind only a match total of 872 when South Africa chased 435 to beat Australia in 2006.

The total of 123 boundaries across both innings - 93 fours and 30 sixes - is also a record in ODIs.

How did England lose this game? At halfway, when Brook left the field arm-in-arm with Will Jacks, the thought of Sri Lanka even getting close to their target seemed highly fanciful.

Yet, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis' decision to chase proved inspired, despite the way his team were dismantled by Brook.

Ultimately, Sri Lanka put the conditions – and Brook's knock – into context, helped by an England team who wilted under the pressure.

They were hampered by the dew, another factor in Sri Lanka's decision to bat second. England made mistakes in the field and their bowlers struggled to grip the ball. Without Archer, they lacked a death bowler.

And, with less then a year to go until the World Cup, England showed no composure as the game began to run away from them.

For as well as Brook batted, his tactics will come into question. Too much faith was placed in Curran, whose 103-2 are the most expensive figures returned by an England bowler in an ODI.

Gus Atkinson opened the bowling and sent down just seven overs of his allotted 10 and Tongue, who almost rescued the game, was only into his ninth.

This tri-series is designed to replicate the tournament conditions England will face at the World Cup in southern Africa. Two games in they are without a win and facing the prospect of needing to beat Pakistan in Lahore on Sunday to stay in the competition.

Brook has become the first man in ODI history to make a double hundred and end up on the losing side.

His strokeplay was irresistible. In a 116-ball stay, he mixed innovation with brutal power and deft touches. He scored all around the ground, clearing the ropes for 10 sixes and adding 21 fours.

A feature of Brook's knock was his measured acceleration. The 27-year-old had only 13 runs from the first 24 deliveries he faced, then upped the pace to reach 50 from 42 balls. His century, his fourth in ODIs, was completed in 75 balls.

It was upon reaching three figures that Brook really cut loose. He went from 100 to 200 in only 39 balls.

As England added 156 in the final 10 overs, Brook passed Stokes' record with a six whipped over the leg side off a full toss bowled by left-arm seamer Dilshan Madushanka.

Whether he was aware of the milestone or not, Brook did not acknowledge his achievement and, in the same over, was dropped at mid-off on 185.

Brook began the final over, delivered by seamer Liyanage, on 186. He clobbered the first ball over the covers for six, then scampered back for two unlikely twos.

Fittingly, the double hundred was reached with a paddled-sweep, then he was caught at third man off the final ball of the innings.

Somehow, it was not enough. Liyanage had the final say.

articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Hosts win by an innings and 31 runs to level series
articles.summary: South Africa break Australia's resistance in the final session a complete a famous victory in the second Test and set up a series decider in Cape Town.
articles.body:
Second Test, Gqeberha (day five of five)

South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81

Australia 99 & 295: Head 121; Rabada 4-77, Mulder 3-64

South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs

South Africa broke Australia's resistance in the final session to complete a famous victory in the second Test and set up a series decider in Cape Town.

Travis Head made 121 for Australia and Scott Boland survived 166 deliveries for 40 runs in an attempt to escape Gqeberha with a draw - the tourists' hopes also boosted by the first session being wiped out by rain.

But the Proteas stuck to their task to take the six wickets needed to win by an innings and 31 runs as the light faded late on the last day.

Premier paceman Kagiso Rabada finished with 4-77 while Marco Jansen, whose 5-33 on day four put South Africa in the ascendancy, took the final wicket as Australia were dismissed for 295.

But all-rounder Wiaan Mulder also played a crucial hand, bowling with accuracy and finding movement off the pitch to dismiss Head, Boland and Australia captain Pat Cummins.

Some of South Africa's great Test wins have come against Australia - notably in the last World Test Championship final two years ago and a Test on this ground in 2018 in the infamous Sandpaper series. This must surely rank highly among them.

They were heavily beaten in the first Test in Durban and when 40-4 and 110-6 in their first innings of this Test, there appeared only one winner in this series.

Instead, the contest has been turned on its head by Bavuma's epic 179 and South Africa twice dismissing Australia, setting up a tantalising finale in Cape Town.

articles.title: James Anderson: Nasser Hussain on England legend not having his Lancashire contract renewed and possible retirement
articles.summary: Former England captain Nasser Hussain reflects on reports that James Anderson’s contract will not be renewed at Lancashire, which would end his 26-year career at his boyhood county and raise questions over the 44-year-old’s future in the sport
articles.body:
Of all the things wrong at Lancashire recently and all the problems they've had, on and off the field, I didn't think Anderson was one of them.

He took 50 wickets at an average of 17 last season and is a Lancashire boy through and through. He's still bowling well and obviously he's had a couple of injuries, but when he has played he has still put in performances.

I remember selecting him for England in 2002 in Australia and we picked him from Lancashire's second team virtually - that's how long he's been there. His longevity is just incredible really for a fast bowler.

I don't know what the financial situation is at Lancashire, so I don't want to comment too much on whether it's right or wrong, but it just didn't seem to me to be the change that you need to make at that club.

If you want to make change, you've got to try and have people like Anderson that take you and help you on that journey. I'm just not sure it's the way you treat such a legend of the club, just not to renew his contract like that.

I'd rather not focus in on how it ended, both for England and for Lancashire - I'd rather be thankful that we've had 26 years of Anderson giving it all for England and Lancashire.

I thought it was a marginal call at best from England to leave him out and retire him the way they did, because they wanted younger bowlers like Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue to come through.

He would have bowled alright in Australia last winter, I tell you. He'd have bowled better than some that bowled out there and he bowled better than some that bowled for Lancashire this summer and have done for the last 26 years.

If Anderson is the problem at Lancashire, I've been watching a different Lancashire over the last few years - he is the last of their problems. I can't believe that he's going to be treated like this and he deserves a bit better.

I'd say most counties in the country would take Anderson, even at the age of 44. When I watched clips of him this summer, he still had that magic about him and the hunger.

His skill is just incredible - the control of the ball, the way he changed from being a swing bowler to a wobble seam bowler and a swing bowler, his hunger, his fitness and his longevity.

Who knows what Anderson will do next, and there's rumours of him retiring, but I'd rather think about the great cricketer that we've had for all those years - and how brilliant he was.

Paul Farbrace has come in at Lancashire as director of cricket and probably wants a clean sweep, to go in a new direction. He's decided that they're going to go into that direction without Anderson.

Lancashire have so underachieved in the last few years and they were second from bottom in Division Two. There's obviously the financial constraints and you want to sign players, but Lancashire and Farbrace have to work out a way of making them back to being a great cricketing side.

If they're going in a change of direction, can they do that with the shadow of one of their greatest ever still being in that dressing room? I would think you would use all the assets Anderson has and all that hunger and all that pride of playing - you'd think that would be an asset to take you in that direction.

I don't want to speak for the members, but I think Lancashire members feel cricket has not become a priority for them. If you get your cricket right, everything generally flows from that, and I personally think Lancashire are a better side with a 44-year-old Anderson than without.

articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Proteas complete emphatic innings-victory to level three-Test series
articles.summary: South Africa won the second Test against Australia by an innings and 31 runs at St George's Park to set up a series decider; Watch the third Test in Cape Town on October 27 live on Sky Sports Cricket
articles.body:
The Proteas won by an innings and 31 runs at St George's Park in Gqeberha to set up a series decider in Cape Town next week.

Australia had won the first Test in Durban by a huge margin, only for South Africa to roar back and answer them in kind.

Despite the morning session being a washout and without one frontline bowler in Anrich Nortje, South Africa bowled out Australia for 295 in its second innings an hour after tea.

The result ties the series at 1-1 and the two sides, currently third and first in the World Test Championship respectively, will play for the series win in Cape Town from Tuesday, live on Sky Sports.

WTC holders South Africa rallied to seemingly save a draw when they wrapped up their rain-affected first innings late on day three after captain Temba Bavuma's 179 and Marco Jansen's rapid 85.

But Australia were then shot out for 99 in their first innings by Jansen's 5-33. They were forced to follow on, and remarkably lost 13 wickets in total on Wednesday. South Africa's pace attack lost Nortje to a suspected groin injury in his fourth over and he didn't bowl for the rest of Australia's second innings.

Australia, resuming the final day on 156-4, still 170 runs behind, hoped on Thursday for a reduced 81 overs of rearguard action with Steve Smith and Alex Carey in reserve but unravelled once chief holdout Travis Head was dismissed.

Wiaan Mulder rebounded from a wicketless and expensive second innings on Wednesday by taking three of the six wickets South Africa needed on the fifth and final day.

Mulder bowled century-maker Head, fellow overnight fighter Scott Boland as well as Australia captain Pat Cummins.

Head, on 87 overnight, posted his 13th Test century with his 12th boundary. But his natural positive intent undid him on 121 when he chopped on against Mulder. Head faced 190 balls.

Smith came in at No 7, three places lower than usual after he got a kink in his neck in the first innings. Mulder tested Smith's neck with a first-ball bouncer.

Smith endured the last five overs of the old ball, but was out for three in the third over of the new ball when he mis-hit pacer Kagiso Rabada. The ball caught the wind and Matthew Breetzke bobbled the ball at midwicket but took it at the second attempt.

Boland passed his previous highest Test score of 21 when he reached tea on 40 with Alex Carey.

But Boland was the seventh Australian out soon after the resumption when he tried to defend a come-backer from Mulder and was beaten between the gates. Boland's resistance lasted for 166 balls to score 40.

Cummins quickly departed, also to Mulder, after hitting a boundary then Rabada returned and took out Mitchell Starc's leg stump with an inside edge.

Jansen completed the victory amid glooming skies when he got Josh Hazlewood to send a thick edge to Aiden Markram at second slip.

Rabada took 4-77, Mulder 3-64, while Jansen finished with six wickets in the match to round off an impressive performance from the hosts.

articles.title: Sri Lanka chase down 430 to stun England in epic ODI tri-series clash despite Harry Brook's historic double century
articles.summary: Janith Liyanage hit a maximum off the penultimate delivery to see Sri Lanka chase down 430 in reply to England's 429-4; Harry Brook fired England's first double hundred in ODI history and overtook Ben Stokes' record score before their stunning defeat
articles.body:
Harry Brook smashed 202 from just 116 deliveries - the fastest double-hundred in ODI history and first ever by an Englishman - before being dismissed from the final ball of the innings, with England's 429-4 their fourth-highest total ever in the 50-over format.

Sri Lanka slipped to 24-2 in reply but were offered hope by a 166-run third-wicket stand between Avishka Fernando (97) and Pavan Rathnayake, who completed an 87-ball century and put on another big partnership with Dasun Shanaka.

Rathnayake was dismissed for 130 and Shanaka fired eight maximums in his 97 from his 50 deliveries, before Janith Liyanage crashed in a 22-ball fifty to leave Sri Lanka needing eight runs from their final over.

Josh Tongue moved momentum back England's way by bowling Dunith Wellalage and Eshan Malinga in successive deliveries, only for Liyanage to fire a six off the penultimate ball and complete a famous victory.

Sri Lanka's successful chase is just the third over 400 in ODI history and gives them their first points of the tri-series tournament, while England's second successive loss is another setback in their bid to reach the final on October 31.

Brook breaks records with huge England knock

England made a positive start after losing the toss and batting first, with Tom Banton racing to his half-century off 48 deliveries and putting on a 74-run opening stand with Ben Duckett.

The left-arm spin of Dunith Wellalage (2-56) removed both openers, as Banton (50) picked out Liyanage in the deep and Duckett (29) was trapped LBW, while Joe Root pushed England forward before Brook's acceleration.

Brook - who felt his side were 'too careful' in the middle overs against Pakistan - was 13 from 24 deliveries when he smashed Kamindu Mendis for successive sixes, with a boundary burst seeing him quickly pass 50 and put on a 159-run stand with Root (69).

Asitha Fernando (1-68) saw Root chip him to mid-wicket but that was not the end of England's onslaught, as Brook and Will Jacks (66 not out) added 185 - including a staggering 156 in the last 10 overs - to post their monster score.

Brook took 39 balls from 100 to reach his double century, with his 31 boundaries - 21 fours and 10 of England's 13 sixes - setting another ODI record, before holing out to Sahan Arachchige off Liyanage (1-32) from the last delivery.

England looked in full control when Tongue bowled Kamindu Mendis (18) and captain Kusal Mendis (0) was run out by Gus Atkinson at the non-striker's end without facing a ball, before Avishka and Rathnayake led Sri Lanka's rebuild.

Avishka was on the verge of his century when he was out caught and bowled by Jamie Overton (1-77), with Sri Lanka still needing 213 from the last 20 overs before an incredible late fightback under the lights.

Rathnayake picked out Banton at long-on to end his impressive 106-ball innings, but Shanaka kept hopes alive by spanking Sam Curran (2-102) for three sixes during a brilliant 20-run over.

Shanaka eventually picked out Banton in the deep off Liam Dawson (1-71) and Curran removed Arachchige (13) after a quick 43-run stand with Liyanage, who ended unbeaten 61 from 27 deliveries to guide Sri Lanka to their epic victory.

Brook on historic knock: 'It doesn't mean anything now!'

England captain Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation:

"It was an incredible game of cricket. I thought both sides were exceptional but Sri Lanka just outplayed us unfortunately.

"We didn't hit our straps with the ball and played to their strengths a little bit. Fair play to them for an incredible achievement.

"It [his 202] was a nice innings. Unfortunately it doesn't mean anything now being on the losing side. It has no value whatsoever.

"We have to go back to the drawing board a little bit. We know where we have gone wrong - we didn't execute well enough with the ball. We have an opportunity in the next couple of games to try and nail down a spot in the final.

"We need to keep things simple and keep our chins up."

articles.title: Harry Brook underlines status as world's best all-format batter in Rawalpindi run-fest
articles.summary: Once the disappointment of defeat dissipates, Harry Brook can reflect on another starring role with the bat which underlines his status as the world's best all-format batter, says Stephan Shemilt.
articles.body:
Just under a year ago, Harry Brook was left wondering if he would be sacked as England white-ball captain and what damage he had done to his international career.

What a turnaround in 12 months. From whacked in Wellington to the run-fest in Rawalpindi, Brook is undeniably England's most important cricketer and probably the best multi-format batter in the world.

Brook's 202 in England's defeat against Sri Lanka was an astonishing display of stroke-making. There can be no higher praise than to compare Brook's dismantling of the Sri Lankan attack to the sort of innings once played by South African genius AB de Villiers.

It was the first double hundred scored by an Englishman in an ODI, passing England's previous best individual score of 182 by Ben Stokes against New Zealand in 2023. In reaching 200 in 114 balls, Brook registered the fastest double ton by anyone in an ODI, bettering the 117 deliveries of India's Shubman Gill against West Indies only last month.

Brook has joined one of international cricket's most exclusive clubs. In completing the set of a hundred in a T20, double hundred in an ODI and triple century in a Test, Brook has matched the previously unique treble of West Indies' legend Chris Gayle.

In the moment, the collection of another landmark might not mean a great deal to Brook. Despite his efforts, his team were beaten as the spirited Sri Lankans pulled off the second-highest run-chase in history in one of the most astonishing ODIs ever played.

For a man who has previously spoken about prioritising match-winning contributions over individual achievements, Brook the captain was left dejected that his innings ultimately counted for nothing. He is the first man to make a double ton in an ODI and end up on the losing side.

Still, it further underlined his status as the premier run-getter across all kinds of international cricket. Perhaps only Australia's Travis Head can challenge Brook for the crown.

Ranked by the International Cricket Council as the best Test batter in the world, Brook averages 53.08 in the longer format of the game. No England player with a minimum of 20 innings since 1968 has a better average than Brook – he stands above Joe Root, Alastair Cook, Geoffrey Boycott, Graham Gooch and everyone else to have batted for England in the past seven decades.

In T20 internationals, Brook averages 36.21 at a strike-rate of 164.92. No batter to have played at least 20 innings for a major nation averages more at a better strike-rate.

Brook is learning to play List A cricket in one-day internationals. Sri Lanka was his 61st List A match, 45 of which have been ODIs. After a slow start to his international 50-over career, Brook averages just under 50 in his past 29 matches and almost 57 in 2026.

The responsibility of captaincy suits him. In ODIs, Brook averages 31 runs more as captain compared to when not. In T20s, his average jumps 19 runs when wearing the metaphorical armband.

Brook's workload is an issue, the Yorkshireman having played in every England fixture since being rested for a T20 series in Ireland last September and, fitness permitting, he will be the only man to play in every game this winter – that's five tours to four countries across three continents. He left home last week and will not again see his own bed until mid-January.

He says his time to rest is during the Indian Premier League, the riches of which he has turned down in order to focus his energy on England. Brook probably does not get enough credit for making such a decision.

There is the question of how good Brook could become. Ben Stokes revealed that, at the end of the Ashes, he took Brook to one side to say he should be averaging 60 or more in Test cricket.

Speaking to the BBC in August, Brook admitted to not being the "finished article".

"I have the ability to hit it everywhere, I just have to figure it out quicker in games," he said.

In terms of improvement, Brook has already shown a willingness to do the hard yards to become a better cricketer.

As a youngster, he struggled with his fitness, but has worked hard to become one of the best athletes in the England team. He has spoken at length about being better able to run twos – he is one of the best runners between the wickets in the world. Brook has also turned himself into one of England's most reliable catchers.

As for the batting, well-qualified judges don't hold back in their praise. Last month, Stokes said Brook may have more talent than Kevin Pietersen. In 2024, James Anderson said Brook could surpass Root as England's highest Test run-scorer. Just last week, Chris Woakes labelled Brook as "next level".

The missing achievement is a starring role in winning a major series or tournament.

Brook's magnificent century should have been enough for England to win the fifth Test against India at The Oval last year, only for him to throw away his wicket with victory in sight. He has not made a century in 10 Ashes Tests against Australia and was only a bit-part player as part of the England team that won the T20 World Cup in 2022.

Maybe his moment is approaching. Next summer is a home Ashes, followed by the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa. Brook will be 28 and at the peak of his powers. There is the chance to play a major part in regaining the urn and to become one of the few British athletes to lift a World Cup in any sport.

To do that, he will have to iron out the flaws that have arisen in England's one-day cricket across the first two matches of the tri-series in Pakistan.

In the opening match, against Pakistan, dropped catches and poor strokes left them well beaten in a contest they could have won.

Against Sri Lanka, England somehow lost from what seemed an impregnable position, their bowling and fielding falling apart amid a growing realisation they were in danger of failing to defend a target of 430.

There was some mitigation. Dew made the ball incredibly slippery, while their attack was weakened by the absence of the rested Jofra Archer and benched Adil Rashid.

Nevertheless, the bowling was awful, particularly Sam Curran, who conceded 103 from nine overs to return the worst figures by an England bowler in an ODI. It was an error by Brook to continue to show faith in the left-armer, while not using the full allocation of 10 overs from either Josh Tongue or Gus Atkinson.

It is one of the first major missteps of Brook's captaincy career and the sort of performance that shows England still have some way to go to be seen as serious World Cup contenders.

Now, England will have to win their next two matches to reach the tri-series final, to be played on 31 October, exactly 12 months on from Brook's horror show in Wellington.

England need the sort of turnaround their captain has managed over the past year

articles.title: What cost England in ODI run-fest vs Sri Lanka as Harry Brook's 'genius' double century has 'no value whatsoever'?
articles.summary: Harry Brook wows Sky pundits Nasser Hussain and Mark Butcher with record-breaking ODI double ton from 114 balls but England end up on losing side after bowling too short and lack of middle-overs wickets; Sam Curran goes at 11.44 runs an over in expensive outing
articles.body:
The ask was a herculean 430, second only to the 438-9 South Africa peeled off versus Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 when it came to successful ODI run chases.

But on a day when South Africa beat Australia once again - this time in a one-sided Test match in Gqeberha - Sri Lanka stunned England in a Rawalpindi run-fest.

That meant Harry Brook's astonishing 202 from 116 balls, during which he reached 200 from 114 deliveries to set a new record for the fastest ODI double ton, came in vain.

So where exactly did things go wrong for England?

Not with the batting, obviously, as Brook's sizzling knock - the highest for England in a men's ODI, eclipsing the 182 Ben Stokes scored against New Zealand in 2023 - was backed up by half-centuries from Tom Banton, Joe Root and Will Jacks.

The bowling was the issue with Sri Lanka rallying from 24-2 once Kamindu Mendis had been bowled by a beauty from Josh Tongue and captain Kusal Mendis was run out backing up without facing a ball after Gus Atkinson tipped on to the non-striker's stumps.

Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain noted how England overcompensated from bowling too full during their 87-run defeat to Pakistan at the same venue on Tuesday by dropping too short, particularly to Pavan Rathnayake, who top-scored with 130 from 106 balls.

The former England captain also lamented his country's long-standing issue of middle-overs wickets, with only one taken between Kusal's run out in the fifth over and Rathnayake holing out off the expensive Sam Curran at long-on in the 41st.

Rathnayake put on 166 with Avishka Fernando for the third wicket and then 133 with the wisely-promoted Dasun Shanaka for the fourth - both of his team-mates made 97.

Hussain: Lack of middle-order wickets a concern for England

Hussain said of the wicketless woes: "It comes from that middle period where England, historically, over the last two or three years, have struggled to take wickets.

"That is even with Adil Rashid, who did not play in this game, at his best, so that is something they need to solve, a box they need to tick. Getting back Jofra Archer, rested for this series, will help and add a bit of firepower.

"Maybe Adil has come off his best but today showed the need for Archer, and Rashid being back to his best. We all big up Adil but he has just dropped off, maybe because of injuries."

Former Sri Lanka batter and Hussain's fellow Sky Sports pundit Kumar Sangakkara said: "England needed an all-out push to take wickets when they had Sri Lanka 24-2. You have 429 on the board.

"Have set plays, try to bowl the bumpers, fielders set for catches - of if you want to restrict because conditions are not suitable for wickets, then go to death bowling early, try to cut off the boundaries.

"The only way they were going to lose the game was by the boundary count rising. If you are a fast bowler, you stop the fours with fields set and the sixes by executing the best deliveries.

"Still, England need to give credit to an incredible batting performance from Sri Lanka."

Sri Lanka get over the line after 'marathon'

That point about Sri Lanka is an important one from Sangakkara.

For as loose as England were with the ball - Curran, in just his second game since The Hundred in August due to a groin injury, struggled to land his moon balls and yorkers and was flogged for 103 runs from his nine overs - Sri Lanka were superb.

They showed grit after slipping two down early, then the ability to adapt by pushing Shanaka up the order - he smoked eight sixes in his 50-ball 97 - and when late wickets had seen Sri Lanka wobble a bit, Janith Liyanage fired under pressure with an unbeaten 61.

Liyanage crunched two fours and a six across three balls off Curran to trim the ask to 29 from 21 deliveries and then spanked the winning six with one ball to spare after Tongue has taken two wickets in two deliveries earlier in the final over.

Hussain added: "Sri Lanka had to be pretty much perfect for 50 overs and they were. There were lads in there who played pretty much the perfect innings.

"It was like running a marathon for Sri Lanka - they saw that last bit and started to stumble when they needed to be calm.

"So Liyanage in the end - that was incredibly special. You looked at his body language, it was like, 'leave it to me, lads' - he was calm, composed and belted it down the ground.

"It was a perfect, historic chase and brilliant for Sri Lanka. They are such a talented, passionate cricketing nation. They needed a day like today and they got one."

Why Brook said his double hundred 'does not matter'

Brook had spoken earlier in the week about wishing there was a match-winning column in players' stats.

If that was part of cricket, then for a long time in Rawalpindi on Thursday it looked like Brook's would have a big fat tick in it.

In the end, though, the Yorkshireman insisted that his individual heroics "didn't matter."

Brook, whose innings featured 21 fours and 10 sixes said: "I always say I want to make match-winning contributions, have a match-winning impact. Unfortunately I've got 200 and it's not been match-winning. In my eyes, it doesn't matter. It had no value whatsoever."

Still, Hussain and Sky Sports colleague Mark Butcher enthused over the England captain, with Hussain calling him the best male multi-format batter in the world and saying his presence makes the team contenders at next year's 50-over World Cup in Africa.

The pundit added: "Every shot selection he made was spot on - it had to be to score 200 that quickly. He has been touched by genius ever since we have seen him.

"The biggest area of growth for this ODI team is if Brook can convert his Test and T20 form into this format. He did that, it was magical.

Butcher said: "Sometimes your breath is taken away with Brook and you don't quite have the words to describe what you are watching.

"Such is his precision and the way he can uses the pace on the ball, he can pretty much manoeuvre it wherever he likes. Then he will fly out of the crease and hit you for six.

"He has such balance, his hands are so good, the control of the bat face is as good as anybody I have seen. He can play a shot for pretty much every delivery. He is absolutely box office."

Now, if England could just get the bowling sorted…

articles.title: James Anderson: Counties keen to speak to seamer after Lancashire exit
articles.summary: James Anderson will have options to extend his legendary playing career after being told he will not be given a new contract by Lancashire.
articles.body:
James Anderson will have options to extend his legendary playing career after being told he will not be given a new contract by Lancashire.

A number of counties are keen to speak to the 44-year-old if he decides to continue playing next summer.

Anderson will leave Old Trafford following Lancashire's decision to release him from the club for whom he first played professionally 25 years ago.

Despite turning 45 in 2027, Anderson, who captained Lancashire last season, was planning on playing for another year before being told he will not be given a new deal.

The exit from Lancashire leaves England's all-time leading wicket-taker with a decision over whether to retire or speak to other counties.

It is understood clubs in both divisions of the County Championship would be interested in negotiating with Anderson and some have already reached out.

Any move for Anderson would likely depend on the finances of the deal, the role he would be offered and the logistics of spending time away from his home in Cheshire.

For a county, the signing of Anderson would represent an acquisition of unmatched quality on and off the field.

Last summer, Anderson was Lancashire's County Championship player of the year, taking 50 wickets in Division Two. Only six other bowlers in the second tier managed more.

It could also lead to the prospect of Anderson transitioning into a coaching role at a new county at the conclusion of his playing career. The opportunity for a club to tap into Anderson's bank of knowledge would be highly appealing.

Listen to the TMS podcast: Is this the end for Jimmy Anderson?

Anderson, 44, not offered new Lancashire contract

On the flipside, there would be an element of risk. Although he remains supremely fit, Anderson's age might mean he is only one injury away from retirement. He has been troubled by calf problems in the latter stages of his career.

Anderson was told of Lancashire's decision by the county's new chief executive Richard Kenyon and director of cricket Paul Farbrace on Monday. The bowler was not offered the opportunity to stay at Old Trafford on reduced terms.

Lancashire have yet to publicly comment, though will hold a forum for the club's members on Monday, when the matter seems certain to be addressed.

Anderson's contract does not officially expire until the end of October and it has been suggested Lancashire would like him to remain involved with the club in some capacity.

However, given how his playing career with Lancashire has been ended, it is far from certain that Anderson would be open to continuing his association with the club he first represented in 2001.

Anderson made his top-level debut playing a List A game for Lancashire Cricket Board against Suffolk in the National Westminster Bank Trophy in 2000.

His debut for Lancashire came a year later in a one-day fixture against Derbyshire.

Anderson began a 22-year international career in 2002. His tally of 704 wickets for England is the third-most by any man in Test history and the most by a pace bowler.

He retired from internationals in 2024 and committed to continuing his career with Lancashire in 2025. At that time, Anderson said he felt he could play for at least three more seasons.

articles.title: Harry Brook breaks Shubman Gill's fastest 200 record as Sri Lanka pull off historic ODI run chase
articles.summary: England captain Harry Brook made history by scoring the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) cricket, but his record-breaking innings
articles.body: England captain Harry Brook made history by scoring the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) cricket, but his record-breaking innings could not prevent Sri Lanka from securing a thrilling two-wicket victory in their tri-series match on Thursday. Sri Lanka chased down a target of 430 with one ball remaining, leaving England at the bottom of the standings after two defeats.Brook reached his double-century in just 114 balls, breaking the previous record of 117 deliveries held by India's Shubman Gill. The 27-year-old also became the first English batter to score an ODI double-century, surpassing Ben Stokes' previous national record of 182 runs.He smashed 202 runs off 116 balls, hitting 21 fours and 10 sixes before being caught by Sahan Arachchige off Janith Liyanage on the final ball of England's innings. Joe Root also contributed with 69 runs off 66 balls as England posted a massive 429-4.Brook, however, was disappointed that his historic achievement ended in defeat."Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn't matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn't even count," Brook said."Heart-breaking. I think you've hit the nail on the head there. It's very disappointing that we haven't been able to defend 430, but that's life, that's cricket," he added.Sri Lanka pull off historic run chaseSri Lanka produced a remarkable batting display to complete the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake led the charge with 130 off 106 balls, while Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both missed their centuries by just three runs.Sri Lanka needed six runs from the final two balls when Liyanage hit Josh Tongue for a six over long-off to seal victory with one delivery remaining. Tongue finished as England's leading wicket-taker with 3-79.Brook praised Sri Lanka's performance and admitted England failed to execute their bowling plans."You don't see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They've played exceptionally well. We couldn't execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they've just played an absolute blinder there ..."England, who lost to Pakistan by 87 runs on Tuesday, now need to win their remaining two matches to keep their hopes of reaching the final in Lahore alive."We'll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. articles.title: Sanju Samson's blazing 67 sets up India's record T20I chase against New Zealand
articles.summary: There were concerns around the Indian team being jetlagged when it arrived at Christchurch’s Hagley Oval for the first T20I against New Zealand on
articles.body: There were concerns around the Indian team being jetlagged when it arrived at Christchurch’s Hagley Oval for the first T20I against New Zealand on Thursday. After all, the team were involved in a T20I series-decider vs West Indies in Bengaluru last Saturday.By the end of the Powerplay in India’s innings, however, it was the hosts who looked dazed as Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma unleashed another of their trademark assaults in pursuit of 226. Samson’s dazzling 67 off 33 balls laid the foundation for India’s highest successful T20I chase, with Naman Dhir’s unbeaten 42 off 15 balls sealing a four-wicket victory with two deliveries to spare.There is a striking simplicity to the way Samson and Abhishek go about their business. Compulsively, they seem to challenge the 100-run mark in the Powerplay. Scoring at least 80-plus, now seems routine. On Thursday, it was Samson who led the charge as India raced to 94/1 in six overs, with Abhishek contributing a brisk 29 off 12 before falling off the penultimate ball of the Powerplay. The significance and impact of Samson’s knock extended beyond just the runs. It bought valuable time for captain Shreyas Iyer to assess the large boundaries and rebuild after India stumbled against Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell.From 93 without loss, India slipped to 122/4, briefly allowing New Zealand to get back into the contest. The hosts hardly helped themselves. Adam Milne and Lockie Ferguson struggled for control, conceding 16 wides, while New Zealand also shelled three catches. By then, Samson and Abhishek had already shaken the home side’s confidence. Every one of Samson’s eight fours and four sixes seemed to drive a dagger in their hearts and hopes. India’s T20 blueprint is now well established. Their openers are encouraged to attack relentlessly, irrespective of the target. “Even if we are chasing 170 and we’ve got off to a flyer, we make sure we kill the game in the Powerplay itself. That’s what we’ve been doing really well in the last couple of years,” Samson said after the match.The high-risk and high-reward approach has the potential to backfire too but Samson stressed about the importance of self-belief and the attitude of keeping the team first at all times. The aggression is tactical rather than reckless. Samson’s greatest strength is his ability to remain composed amid the chaos. He rarely appears rushed, even while dismantling bowling attacks. Against New Zealand, he dealt comfortably with the short-ball ploy before unfurling a series of clean straight hits that left the bowlers searching for answers. Standing slightly leg-side of the ball, he created room to access different parts of the ground without sacrificing shape or balance.Brief scores: New Zealand 225/4 in 20 overs (Finn Allen 45, Glenn Phillips 82 n.o.; Mayank Yadav 1-40) lost to India 230/6 in 19.4 overs (Sanju Samson 67, Shreyas Iyer 42, Naman Dhir 42 n.o; Michael Bracewell 2-37).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Naman Dhir emerges as India's answer to middle-order conundrum
articles.summary: Naman Dhir had been waiting for a proper opportunity with the bat during his West Indies white-ball tour of India.
articles.body: Naman Dhir had been waiting for a proper opportunity with the bat during his West Indies white-ball tour of India. While he impressed with his tidy off-spin on batting-friendly surfaces, meaningful time in the middle was hard to come by. His breakthrough came in the final T20I in Bengaluru last Saturday, when he smashed an unbeaten 24 off just six balls before rain brought an early end to the match. Five days later, on the other side of the globe, Dhir further strengthened his credentials, guiding India to victory with an unbeaten 42 off 15 balls against New Zealand in Christchurch.Ever since the 2019 ODI World Cup, India have been searching for a middle-order batter capable of contributing valuable overs with the ball. The team's dependence on Hardik Pandya as a seam-bowling all-rounder and the gradual decline of Ravindra Jadeja's role left a noticeable gap, particularly in SENA conditions. Axar Patel and Washington Sundar were both tried, but neither managed to make the role their own over an extended period.At the start of 2026, Riyan Parag, before his hamstring injury, and Ayush Badoni appeared ahead in the pecking order. In the space of a month, however, Dhir has surged to the front of the queue. Seen as Ajit Agarkar's final major selection punt before stepping down as chairman of selectors, the Mumbai batter is quietly making a strong case for himself."He gives us a lot of options, especially against left-handers with his off-spin, and even against right-handers on certain surfaces. Those two or three crucial overs can change the momentum of a game," India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer said after Thursday's opening T20I. "The calm and composure he showed with the bat was magnificent."To be fair, both Axar and Washington have delivered whenever called upon. articles.body: MUMBAI: Mumbai's opener and newly-appointed vice-captain Ayush Mhatre, who suffered from a recurrence of his right hamstring (Grade 4 tear) injury recently, underwent surgery on Thursday at the at the Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital here, with India's sports orthopedic Mumbai-based surgeon Dr Dinshaw Pardiwala doing the job, TOI has learnt."Ayush underwent a 90-minute surgery for 'Hamstring Grade 4 tear repair,' for a recurrent injury on right hamstring. He was operated upon by Dr Dinshaw Pardiwala. He is comfortable and walking. He will be discharged today evening," a source tracking developments told this paper on Friday."He will be out of action for four months," the source added. It means that the 19-year-old batter is unlikely to play for Mumbai the remainder of the 2026-27 season.Pardiwala has has helped some of the biggest names in in Team India (he has operated upon Rishabh Pant, Jasprit Bumrah, Ravindra Jadeja and many other top cricketers) and Olympic sports (Olympic medal winners Neeraj Chopra, Vinesh Phogat, PV Sindhu) to overcome injuries and return to match fitness.The 19-year-old batter’s right hamstring injury recurred during Mumbai's innings and 155 run win over Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium in their opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. articles.body: South Africa's innings-and-31-run victory over Australia in the second Test in Gqeberha has made the race for the World Test Championship (WTC) final more competitive.Although Australia remain at the top of the standings, the defeat stops them from extending their lead and gives other teams, including India, some hope.Australia have a points percentage (PCT) of 75.00, while New Zealand are second at 72.22 and South Africa sit third at 66.67.What India need to doIndia are currently fifth in the standings, with seven Tests remaining in the cycle — two against New Zealand and five against Australia at home. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand. The 21-year-old will replace KL Rahul, who will join the ODI squad after playing the first four-day match against New Zealand A, starting on Saturday at Bert Sutcliffe Oval at Lincoln University.The southpaw has continued his red-hot form with back-to-back hundreds in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season. Shikhar smashed 143 against Kerala in Jamshedpur and then scored a match-saving 127 against Maharashtra in Pune.Shikhar's mentor, Ishank Jaggi, a former Jharkhand cricketer, has heaped praise on the youngster, saying the time is absolutely ripe for him to take the next step."It is perfect timing. He is in good form. Scored two centuries in Ranji. Had a great Duleep Trophy final and Irani Trophy as well," Jaggi told TimesofIndia.com.After an excellent debut season in 2025-26, in which he amassed 613 runs at an average of 55.73, including two centuries, he has started the new season in rollicking fashion, smashing 143 in Jharkhand's opening match against Kerala at the Keenan Stadium in Jamshedpur.The southpaw also made some valuable contributions in the Duleep Trophy final for East Zone, scoring 85 and 52 in the two innings, followed by a solid 60 on a green top in Srinagar in the Irani Trophy, playing for Rest of India against defending Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir.Jaggi, who is currently coaching the Jharkhand U-23 side, says Shikhar Mohan has been in top form for the past four to five years."Look, he has been in good form for the last four to five years. He has dominated age-group cricket as well. I feel this is a great time for him to have this experience. It will be great exposure for him. He will realise what he needs to add to his game and will come back as a better cricketer," says Jaggi, who has played 90 First Class matches.Jaggi is correct about the southpaw's rich vein of form. Shikhar Mohan enjoyed significant success with the Under-23 side in the Col CK Nayudu Trophy. In the 2023-24 season, he scored 623 runs, including two hundreds and three fifties. He continued his run-scoring spree the following season, scoring 887 runs, which helped him earn a call-up to the senior side.One issue with Shikhar's batting, which the youngster himself has admitted to, is his inability to convert starts into big scores, something he is working on with Jaggi."In my first year of Under-19 cricket, I scored around 550 runs, with most of my scores in the 70s and 80s. The following year, I wanted to focus more and convert those starts into bigger scores," he had told this website."Before facing a ball, I talk to myself. I remind myself to watch the ball and stay focused. That has helped me a lot. Jaggi bhai also helped me with this, especially when he was with the Under-19 team. I started concentrating more and focusing on one ball at a time. That approach has really helped me," he added.Ishank, however, feels the mental block is something even the game's greats have faced."Everyone has gone through that phase. But you have to understand that he is scoring those 70s and 80s consistently, which is no small achievement. He is still raw and can be groomed, and that's why I said this call has come at the right time," he said.Shikhar will travel to New Zealand on October 26 and will link up with the India A squad in Christchurch, where the second four-day game will be played from October 31.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Harry Brook produced an innings for the ages, becoming only the second cricketer after West Indies legend Chris Gayle to score a triple-century in Tests,
articles.body: Harry Brook produced an innings for the ages, becoming only the second cricketer after West Indies legend Chris Gayle to score a triple-century in Tests, a double-century in ODIs and a century in T20Is. However, the England captain's historic achievement ended in heartbreak as Sri Lanka pulled off a stunning chase of 430 runs to win the ODI tri-series encounter by two wickets with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi.Brook smashed 202 off just 116 balls, including 21 fours and 10 sixes, to become the first English batter to score an ODI double-century. He reached the landmark in only 114 deliveries, breaking the record for the fastest double-century in men's ODI cricket. His breathtaking knock propelled England to a formidable 429/4, but even that proved insufficient against a determined Sri Lankan batting unit.Brook joins Gayle in elite multi-format clubBrook's extraordinary innings completed a rare international cricket milestone. The 27-year-old had previously scored 317 against Pakistan in a Test match at Multan in October 2024 and registered a T20I century, including an unbeaten 114 against Sri Lanka in September 2026. His 202 against Sri Lanka added the ODI double-century to that remarkable list.Gayle had long been the only player to achieve the feat, having scored 317 against South Africa and 333 against Sri Lanka in Test cricket, 215 against Zimbabwe in ODIs and 117 against South Africa in a T20I.Fastest ODI double-century and first for EnglandBrook's 202 was historic on several fronts. He became England's first-ever men's ODI double-centurion, surpassing Ben Stokes' previous national record of 182 against New Zealand in 2023.He reached 200 off 114 balls, three deliveries faster than the previous record of 117. Brook's innings gathered momentum after a measured start, with the England captain accelerating through the middle and death overs to dismantle Sri Lanka's bowling attack.He also shared a 159-run partnership with Joe Root, who scored 69, before combining with Will Jacks for a rapid stand that helped England add 156 runs in the final 10 overs. Jacks remained unbeaten on 66 off 30 balls as England posted 429/4.Sri Lanka pull off historic chase to spoil Brook's nightDespite Brook's record-breaking effort, Sri Lanka produced a remarkable response to complete the second-highest successful run chase in men's ODI history.Pavan Rathnayake led the pursuit with a superb 130, while Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both scored 97.
