articles.summary: India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has stressed the importance of trusting his process and staying focused on his game despite the criticism and
articles.body: India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has stressed the importance of trusting his process and staying focused on his game despite the criticism and opinions that come with playing for the national team. His comments came after India chased down 230/6 with two balls remaining to record their highest-ever successful run chase in T20I cricket, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the opening match of the five-game series.Samson said he does not play to silence critics. Instead, he focuses on his preparation, keeps things simple and avoids letting social media reactions affect his mindset.“To be very honest, you can’t focus on what people on social media or others are saying. You have to stay committed to the process and create the right environment for yourself. Playing for Indian cricket is not easy, with so much noise and so many people having their own opinions. But I don’t play this game with the mindset of proving anyone wrong. I keep my cricket at the forefront, trust my process, respect my practice and focus on doing the best I can. I like to keep things simple and stay focused on what I can control, rather than letting outside opinions influence my mindset,” Samson told reporters after the match.Samson backs India's aggressive approachSamson played a key role in the chase, scoring 67 off 33 balls to give India a strong start. However, a middle-order collapse put the team under pressure before Naman Dhir struck an unbeaten 42 off just 15 deliveries to seal the victory.Samson credited India's attacking approach across the powerplay, middle overs and final overs for helping the team achieve the record chase. He said the team has continued to back this style of cricket since winning the 2024 T20 World Cup.“We approach the powerplay, middle overs and death overs very differently. Even when chasing 170, if we get off to a flying start, we make sure we try to finish the game in the powerplay itself. That’s something we’ve been doing really well over the last couple of years,” Samson said.He added that India must continue trusting their approach, even when it does not always produce the desired results.Samson said the team's priority is to build on what works, play to their strengths and put the team's interests first. articles.title: 93 fours, 552 boundary runs! All the major records as Sri Lanka pull off historic ODI chase against England
articles.summary: Sri Lanka pulled off one of the greatest run chases in one-day international history, overhauling England's 429/4 with a remarkable 430/8 to register an
articles.body: Sri Lanka pulled off one of the greatest run chases in one-day international history, overhauling England's 429/4 with a remarkable 430/8 to register an extraordinary two-wicket victory in Rawalpindi on Thursday. The 430-run chase was the second-highest successful run chase in ODI cricket, behind South Africa's famous pursuit of 435 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006.The extraordinary contest produced records at both ends, with England captain Harry Brook smashing a historic 202 before Sri Lanka responded with a batting assault of their own. The match aggregate of 859 runs was the second-highest in ODI history, behind the 872-run Johannesburg classic between Australia and South Africa in 2006.Sri Lanka's victory also marked only the third successful 400-plus chase in ODI cricket, following South Africa's 2006 triumph and India's pursuit of 406 against West Indies in Guwahati last month.Highest successful chases in ODIs435 - SA vs Aus Joburg 2006430 - SL vs Eng Rawalpindi 2026406 - Ind vs WI Guwahati 2026375 - Net vs WI Harare 2023 (Super Over win)372 - SA vs Aus Durban 201693 fours, 552 boundary runs rewrite ODI record booksThe Rawalpindi run fest set a new benchmark for boundaries in an ODI, with the two sides smashing a combined 93 fours and 30 sixes. The 93 fours eclipsed the previous record of 87, set during the Australia-South Africa match in Johannesburg in 2006.The teams accumulated 552 runs through boundaries, comprising 93 fours and 30 sixes, surpassing the previous record of 532 boundary runs — 64 fours and 46 sixes — in the West Indies-England ODI at St George's in 2019.England struck 48 fours, equalling the joint second-highest tally by a team in an ODI, while Sri Lanka contributed 45. The match aggregate of 859 also became the highest in a List A game in Asia, going past the previous mark of 825.Sri Lanka's 430/8 was their second-highest ODI total, behind the 443/9 they posted against the Netherlands in Amstelveen in 2006.Highest match aggregate in an ODI872 - Aus (434) vs SA (438) Joburg 2006859 - Eng (429) vs SL (430) Rawalpindi 2026825 - Ind (414) vs SL (411) Rajkot 2009811 - WI (405) vs Ind (406) Guwahati 2026807 - Eng (419) vs WI (389) St George’s 2019Brook's historic double century ends in defeatBrook became the first England batter to score an ODI double century, reaching the milestone in 114 balls before finishing with 202 off 116 deliveries. His innings was the highest individual score in an ODI defeat, surpassing Charles Coventry's unbeaten 194 for Zimbabwe against Bangladesh in 2009.Brook's knock powered England to 429/4, with Joe Root scoring 69, Tom Banton making 50 and Will Jacks remaining unbeaten on 66. Brook's 202 also made him the first batter to score a double century in an ODI and finish on the losing side."It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes," Brook said after the defeat.Highest scores in a losing cause in ODIs202 - Harry Brook vs Eng Rawalpindi 2026194* - Charles Coventry vs Ban Bulawayo 2009193 - Fakhar Zaman vs SA Joburg 2021191 - Goerge Munsey vs Net Dundee 2025181* - Matthew Hayden vs NZ Hamilton 2007Sri Lanka's late assault seals an unforgettable winSri Lanka's chase was built around Avishka Fernando's 97 and Pavan Rathnayake's 130 off 106 balls. Their 166-run third-wicket partnership revived the innings after Sri Lanka lost two early wickets. Rathnayake then added 133 runs with Dasun Shanaka, who smashed 97 off 50 balls.Dunith Liyanage's unbeaten 61 off just 27 deliveries kept Sri Lanka in the contest after Shanaka's dismissal. Sri Lanka scored 170 runs in the final 15 overs, the highest total recorded in the last 15 overs of an ODI with available ball-by-ball data, eclipsing West Indies' 146 against England in North Sound in 2023.Needing six runs from the final two balls, Janith Liyanage finished the contest in spectacular fashion by launching Josh Tongue over long-off for a six. The result handed England a second successive defeat in the Pakistan tri-series and gave Sri Lanka a victory to remember.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: BCCI appoints former India pacer Parvinder Awana as Junior Selection Committee chairperson
articles.summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday appointed former India pacer Parvinder Awana as the chairperson of its Junior Selection
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday appointed former India pacer Parvinder Awana as the chairperson of its Junior Selection Committee."The Cricket Advisory Committee (CAC) conducted a selection process for the appointment of members to the Junior Cricket Committee. The CAC screened and interviewed applicants and, following the process, recommended the appointment of Parvinder Awana as Chairman, along with Krishna Das, Rakesh Patel and N. Arjun Yadav as members of the Committee," BCCI said in a statement.Awana played two T20Is for India and featured in 62 First-Class matches, taking 191 wickets. He represented Delhi, India A and Rest of India during his playing career and also played in the IPL for Kings XI Punjab. After retiring, he moved into coaching and worked with Delhi's U16, U19 and U23 teams, as well as India U19 and various BCCI and Centre of Excellence (COE) high-performance programmes.Krishna Das, a former fast bowler who represented Assam and Goa, played 49 First-Class matches and took 166 wickets. He also represented India U19 and India A before moving into coaching. Das later served as the bowling coach of the India U19 team and the Uttarakhand Ranji Trophy side.Rakesh Patel represented Gujarat and Baroda and played for India A. He also featured in the Duleep Trophy, Deodhar Trophy and Irani Trophy. After his playing career, Patel coached Baroda and Gujarat teams across the U19, U23 and senior levels. He was the head coach of the Baroda U23 team in the 2025-26 season.N. Arjun Yadav represented India A and played 83 First-Class matches. He was also part of India's U19 World Cup-winning squad in 2000. After playing for Hyderabad, Yadav took up coaching and went on to serve as head coach of the Hyderabad senior and U23 teams. He has also worked as a BCCI match referee since 2022.The BCCI said the fifth member of the Junior Cricket Committee will be appointed shortly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Temba Bavuma turned away during Steve Smith's catch in second Test? South Africa captain explains viral reaction
articles.summary: South Africa registered a historic win over Australia in the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha on Thursday.
articles.body: South Africa registered a historic win over Australia in the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha on Thursday. The Proteas declared their first innings at 425/9 before bowling Australia out for 99 and enforcing the follow-on. Australia fought to save the match in their second innings but were dismissed for 295, handing South Africa an innings and 31-run victory. The win helped Temba Bavuma and Co level the three-match Test series 1-1.Bavuma was named Player of the Match for his career-best knock of 179, which helped South Africa build a big lead. The Proteas captain also gave fans and commentators a laugh with his reaction to a catch during Australia's second innings.The incident took place in the 83rd over when Steve Smith attempted a big shot against Kagiso Rabada but managed only a thick top edge. The ball went high into the air, and Matthew Breetzke, positioned at mid-wicket, initially fumbled the catch before holding on to give South Africa a crucial breakthrough.Replays later showed Bavuma turning his face towards the crowd as Breetzke tried to complete the catch, seemingly unable to watch the moment unfold. His reaction left the commentators laughing.Speaking at the post-match press conference, Bavuma explained that he had been nervous because of the windy conditions and understood how important Smith's wicket was for South Africa."I was very nervous at that time. High catches here at St George's can be tough, especially when the wind is blowing like that. I couldn't see who was under the catch. So, definitely it's not a case of me not having any faith in that individual," he said."It just felt like a big moment in the game. Steve Smith, what an important cog he is withing their batting lineup. I think I just kind of allowed my emotions to get better of me there," he added.Bavuma's innings of 179 laid the foundation for a victory that had appeared unlikely after rain washed out the first two days. South Africa were also in trouble on the third morning after being asked to bat first.Despite the win, Bavuma said the team would not get carried away, with the final Test scheduled to begin in five days."There's still a job at hand with another match still to go," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Naman Dhir's rise: How the 'jugaadu' cricketer carved his space
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: When the selectors sprung a surprise by picking Naman Dhir for the West Indies series, eyebrows were raised and scepticism followed.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When the selectors sprung a surprise by picking Naman Dhir for the West Indies series, eyebrows were raised and scepticism followed. But the Punjab all-rounder is slowly and steadily making a compelling case for himself with performances suggesting his selection may not have been as out of the blue as it seemed.Dhir has dealt with scepticism and scrutiny right from his early days as a cricketer. So much so that, after being repeatedly overlooked by the Punjab selectors in 2021, he decided to pack his bags and move to Edmonton, Canada, where his sister lives. However, an assurance from his father, Naresh Dhir, and his late coach, Gagan Sidhu, convinced him to continue for one more year. Things changed rapidly for the all-rounder who always had the uncanny ability to break into a set-up after carefully analysing the right opening.Dhir's childhood friend Sahaj Dhawan, who is currently part of the Punjab Ranji Trophy team, shares an interesting anecdote which beautifully sums up the journey. The two have played together since they were 12 and "jugaad" has always been the undertone."Faridkot is considered a minor district (second tier) in the Punjab Cricket Association's (PCA) inter-district tournaments for all age groups. Naman used to see at which position the selectors were looking for a batter in the line-up. He used to bat at that position. He has played at every position possible," laughs Dhawan.This adaptability might be why Mumbai Indians (MI) used the Right to Match (RTM) card to sign him for Rs 5.25 crore in the 2024 IPL mega auction and now use him as a floater in their batting line-up.Before making his India debut, Dhir had played only a handful of matches, but his impact with the bat and his ability to bowl impressed the team management. Playing for Amritsar Soormas, the 26-year-old smashed 655 runs in 10 games at a strike rate of 217.61, with a highest score of 173, in the Sher-e-Punjab T20 League.His exploits in the tournament caught the attention of none other than Shubman Gill, and it is learnt that the Indian captain backed his inclusion in the squad and handed him his debut cap in Thiruvananthapuram.Dhawan says he and Dhir had promised each other that no matter what, they would cheer for each other when either played for India. However, Dhawan could not keep his promise of being there in person when his friend made his debut.Whenever I have texted him 'all the best', he has played well. Now, I have decided that I will do it before every match. Long may this tradition continue."Mai ja nahi paaya (I couldn't go)," says Dhawan.He adds: "I had a Ranji Trophy trial match on that day. We were playing against Punjab U-23. I scored 150, and that's how I got picked for the Punjab Ranji team. He knew about it and told me to focus on the trial. Naman was over the moon when I got picked."Dhawan further adds that he has made it a ritual to wish Naman good luck on every match day, and it seems to be working."Ek totka hai humara (There is a superstition we follow). Whenever I have texted him 'all the best', he has played well. Now, I have decided that I will do it before every match. Long may this tradition continue," laughs Dhawan.Meanwhile, back in Faridkot, Naman's father, Naresh, who worked at a chemist's shop, has retired and is enjoying a celebrity status."I am retired now. Naman forced me to retire, and he was right as well. I am 67 now. I can't work twelve hours a day," says Dhir Sr."I have watched his matches in the IPL, and we all went to Chandigarh to watch him play against the West Indies. Watching him in the Indian jersey was special. I hope he continues to do well and win many more matches for our country," he adds.Naresh Dhir credits Naman's late first coach, Gagan Sidhu, for everything his son has achieved."Gagan always used to say, 'Dhir paji, Naman will play for India.' Now, sadly, he is not alive to see him playing for India," says Dhir.Gagan was only 36 when he passed away due to multiple organ failure. He left behind a very young family, and Naman, along with Sahaj, is doing his bit to support them."He taught us everything. Gagan paji was like an elder brother to us. He used to fight with the selectors for us. His son is very young. He is our responsibility now. We want to be an elder brother to him, just like his father was to us," says Dhawan.Waheguru mehar kare, te tu tarakki kare (May Waheguru bless you and may you continue to prosper). This is what I told him over the call last evening."Gagan paji was very dedicated towards us. Naman ne toh bahot chaante khaaye hain unse, bahut maar padi hai usey, ek baar toh bat se bhi (Naman was punished by him several times. He got beaten up quite a bit, once even with a bat)," recalls Dhawan.The cricketing world has been praising Naman Dhir for his calm demeanour, but Dhawan is not surprised by the attention his friend is receiving."When he is batting, he is very calm. But he is temperamental when I am batting. Agar mai jaldi out ho jau toh gaaliyan deta hai, aisa shot kyu maara, waise kyu maara (If I get out early, he hurls abuses at me, asking, 'Why did you play that shot? Why did you play it that way?')," says Dhawan.Dhawan has just one message for his friend, whose journey he has witnessed from close quarters."Waheguru mehar kare, te tu tarakki kare (May Waheguru bless you and may you continue to prosper). This is what I told him over the call last evening," he says.Dhir's journey is a reminder that there is more than one way to make it in cricket. From figuring out where the selectors needed a batter and adapting his game to fit the role, to embracing the demands of being a floater in Mumbai Indians' line-up, he has found ways to keep moving forward.That ability to improvise, or jugaad, has been matched by a zindadil spirit that has kept him going through years of rejection and uncertainty. The sample size is still small, but with his unbeaten 15-ball 42 at picturesque Hagley Oval, Dhir has shown that he has all the shots in his arsenal to become the finisher India need in white-ball cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli ignored calls, messages after promising India comeback: Amit Mishra makes huge claim
articles.summary: Former India leg-spinner Amit Mishra believes an injury during the 2017 T20I against England in Bengaluru may have brought his international career to an
articles.body: Former India leg-spinner Amit Mishra believes an injury during the 2017 T20I against England in Bengaluru may have brought his international career to an early end. Mishra, who never played for India again after that match, claimed that then head coach Anil Kumble and captain Virat Kohli had assured him of a comeback once he regained full fitness. However, he alleged that Kohli stopped responding to his calls and messages after he recovered.Mishra made these claims during an episode of a podcast hosted by former India cricketer Aakash Chopra. He said the assurances from Kumble and Kohli did not translate into a return to the national team, with the match against England eventually becoming his final international appearance for India."I got my leg injured during that time in Bangalore. And when I was leaving after getting injured, Anil Kumble was the coach. So I told Anil Bhai, I said, 'Anil Bhai...'. He said, 'Don't worry. As soon as you get fit, you will automatically come back,'" Mishra claimed during the podcast.He said he also spoke to Kohli, who had taken over as captain, and received a similar assurance about his place in the team."Then, Virat Kohli became the captain after this. I also asked Virat Kohli, I said, 'Brother, what needs to be done?' He said, 'You don't worry. Get fully fit and comfortable, and you are there [in the team],'" he added.Mishra said that after recovering from the injury, he contacted Kohli to ask about his chances of returning to the Indian team. According to the leg-spinner, Kohli told him he would provide an update within seven to 10 days, but Mishra claimed he never heard back from the former India captain."So, I went to him. I asked, 'Brother, what's the situation?' So he said, 'I will let you know in a week to ten days.' Then brother, one week passed, two weeks passed, three weeks passed, there was absolutely no update from him. I called him... so, he did not pick up the call. I messaged him, but there was no reply," Mishra said, accusing Kohli of failing to keep his promise.Mishra also said that several other players who had suffered more serious injuries and spent longer periods on the sidelines returned to the national team once they were fit. He felt he was not given the same opportunity and said he had never received an explanation for what happened."I called again, he did not answer. I called twice more, still nothing... so I also let it go. Then I thought, 'Brother, what can we do?' When someone does not want you, what can you do? When players who got more severely injured than you, and were injured for much longer, made their comebacks... yet, I have never received any answer to this day."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India top-order batter S Meghana announced her retirement from all forms of cricket on Friday at the age of 30. The Andhra Pradesh cricketer last represented India in October 2022 and played in the Women's Premier League (WPL) for Gujarat Giants and Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB).Meghana announced her decision in a post on Instagram, thanking the game for the experiences and relationships she had built during her career. She also said she intended to remain connected to cricket and work towards helping the next generation of players."As I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket as a player, my heart is overflowing with gratitude," Meghana wrote in an Instagram post."The field has been my second home, teaching me resilience, humility, and giving me memories and friendships that I will carry for a lifetime," she wrote."While my cricket days come to an end, my bond with cricket will never break. I will always stay deeply connected to the game and intend to dedicate my life to giving back to the sport, mentoring the next generation, and serving the game that gave me everything," she added.Meghana made her T20I debut against the West Indies in Vijayawada in November 2016, scoring 17 off 16 balls in a 31-run defeat. She made her ODI debut against New Zealand in Queenstown in February 2022, scoring four off 14 balls.She found her rhythm in the next two matches of that series, scoring 49 off 50 balls and 61 off 41 balls. However, those three matches remained her only ODI appearances, in which she scored a total of 114 runs.In 17 T20Is, Meghana scored 258 runs at a strike rate of 102.78, including one half-century. She scored a half-century in both the ODI and T20I formats during her international career.Meghana also played three seasons of the WPL, beginning with Gujarat Giants before joining RCB, where she spent two years. She was part of the Bengaluru franchise's title-winning squad in 2024. Her last appearance in the league came during the 2025 season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pratika Rawal's century, Shree Charani's four-for power India to nine-wicket win over Zimbabwe in first WODI
articles.summary: Pratika Rawal scored her third ODI century while Shree Charani claimed career-best figures of 4/23 as India defeated Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the
articles.body: Pratika Rawal scored her third ODI century while Shree Charani claimed career-best figures of 4/23 as India defeated Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the opening match of the three-ODI series in Vadodara on Friday.Zimbabwe were bowled out for 197 despite a half-century from Beloved Biza, with Charani and Kranti Gaud (3/42) leading India's bowling effort. Pratika then guided the chase with an unbeaten 100 as India reached 200/1 in 27.1 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the series.Pratika struck 15 fours in her 100 not out, scoring at a strike rate of over 100. The right-hander relied on shots along the ground and did not take unnecessary risks while batting on a pitch that offered little assistance to the bowlers.Pratika's opening partner Mandhana scored 32 before being caught by Biza at long-on off Olinder Chare in the 16th over, ending a 94-run opening partnership.Shafali, who came to bat at No. 3, continued her attacking approach and remained unbeaten on 64 off 33 balls, hitting five fours and four sixes.Earlier, Charani helped restrict Zimbabwe to 197 on a batting-friendly pitch at Kotambi. The left-arm spinner dismissed openers Modester Mupachikwa, who scored 25, and Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano (21) before returning to remove Nyasha Gwanzura (13) and Michelle Mavunga (29).Kranti Gaud supported Charani with three wickets for 42 runs as India kept Zimbabwe from building substantial partnerships. Biza was the visitors' top scorer, making 62 off 92 balls with five fours. She held one end together during the innings.India's bowling effort was, however, accompanied by several fielding errors, including dropped catches.In the third over, Mugeri-Tiripano edged a delivery from Gaud while attempting a drive outside off stump, but wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh failed to hold on to the catch.Mupachikwa offered another chance in the eighth over when she attempted to pull a wide delivery from Gaud and edged it towards Deepti Sharma at second slip. The India vice-captain tried to take the catch with a reverse cup, but the ball popped out of her hands.Mavunga also benefited from a dropped catch while scoring quick runs. In the 40th over, Gaud failed to hold on to a difficult chance at deep midwicket off Deepti's bowling.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gujarat Titans player added to India squad as cover for injured Ishan Kishan for second New Zealand T20I
articles.summary: Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra has been added to India's squad for the second T20I against New Zealand as cover for Ishan Kishan, who has
articles.body: Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra has been added to India's squad for the second T20I against New Zealand as cover for Ishan Kishan, who has been ruled out of Saturday's match due to an injury.Kishan suffered a low-grade right adductor strain during the opening match of the five-T20I series, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirmed on Friday."Wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan sustained a low-grade right adductor strain during the first T20I against New Zealand and is ruled out of the second T20I to be played on Saturday," the BCCI said."The Men’s Selection Committee has added Kumar Kushagra to the squad as cover for the second T20I. Kushagra, who is currently in Christchurch with the India A squad, will join the India squad for the second T20I. The BCCI Medical Team continues to monitor Kishan’s progress," the board added.Kushagra was part of the India A squad set to face New Zealand A in a three-match unofficial Test series beginning on Saturday in Lincoln. He will now join the senior team for the second T20I at Hagley Oval in Christchurch.Kishan has scored 1,955 runs in 67 T20Is at an average of 31.03 and a strike rate of 148.55. He remains part of India's squad for the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand.India lead the T20I series 1-0 after winning the opening match by four wickets. Sanju Samson top-scored in the chase with 67 off 33 balls, while Naman Dhir struck an unbeaten 42 off just 15 deliveries to help India reach the target with two balls to spare. Captain Shreyas Iyer also scored 42 off 28 balls.Earlier, Glenn Phillips made an unbeaten 82 off 40 balls and Finn Allen scored 45 off 24 deliveries as New Zealand posted 225/4, their highest total in home T20Is.India's tour of New Zealand includes five T20Is, followed by five ODIs and two Test matches.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
